seal.statement: Per-node serve eligibility is one fact with one owner: the control-plane readiness owner answers it from a committed read of the nodes rows (status, boot incarnation, ready lease) and the latest published control_plane_publications row (publication epoch, published active nodes, priority spread) taken on the raft leaders of those system partitions, as {decision, epoch} or a typed UNAVAILABLE{reason, epoch, retryAfterMs}; the readiness snapshot is a memo keyed by that epoch and a stale memo answers UNAVAILABLE_STALE{epoch}. User-table routing, CREATE TABLE provisioning (complete at the sealed quorum minimum with a typed under_replicated outcome naming the epoch and missing count, or PROVISIONING_UNAVAILABLE mapped to SQLSTATE 57P03), the rebalancer's critical-topology settle, available-node and local-serve decisions, the in-flight operations source and the learner count check consume that answer or the committed lease it is built from. System-table routing decides on raft leadership and live transport, never on serve eligibility, so no readiness carve-out is needed. Deleted: the system-table leader fail-open and its inline evidence-absent set, readiness-denial-classification.js, the priority-recovery bootstrap routing bypass and its read lane, the fresh-bootstrap routing grace, every !== false and empty-means-satisfied default on a readiness input, allowStaleOnCacheChange and maxCachedAgeMs on decision paths, the degraded provisioning fallback, the provisioning convergence poll and its 10 s constant, the transient-shortfall minimum lowering, and the CACHE source of in-flight topology operations. On a fresh three-node formation the serve lane opens on every node.

text: Lead guardrails for attempt 1 (2026-11-02): (1) the system-table structural route (active+addressed+live transport) is only the candidate hint; correctness comes from the target's leader witness (leader-required reads, enforceRequiredLeaderReadAuthority) or its typed redirect / NOT_LEADER (writes, partition-service-remote-query-methods.js:82-103), followed by query-executor-partition-delivery.js:446-512 without consulting readiness; witnessed in test/query/query-executor-serve-eligibility-routing.test.js (stale cached leader). (2) every non-serve dimension still gating a user table after attempt 1 is listed in the attempt note. (3) isBootstrapRoutingGraceWindow's status is recorded explicitly.

R17 finding (guardrail 3): isBootstrapRoutingGraceWindow (query-executor-partition-service-resolution.js; bootstrap-topology-snapshot-owner-leader-identity.js:15) is not a timer: it names the phase 'partitions row never updated since creation' (created_at === updated_at) and, with an empty leader_node_id, lets getFreshBootstrapLeaderServices order the service-role rows to try first for a write. It changes only the candidate order (a hint); the target's redirect or NOT_LEADER decides. The fact it names is the partitions row's own field pair, read through the cache as a hint. Owner: query routing with the partition-leader metadata owner (Group B area); strain: R11 (a projected row orders candidates), acceptable under D2 as hint-only; no decision is made from it.

Guardrail 2 result (attempt 1): in production no non-serve readiness dimension gates the routing of a user table: resolveTableRoutingReadinessDimension (sql-query-engine.js:397-413) and resolveTransactionOperationRoutingReadinessDimension (:348-355) route every user partition on SERVE_ELIGIBLE (now the owner answer); every other dimension passed (CONTROL_PLANE_RECOVERY_ELIGIBLE in the system gateway, replica-operation repository, CDC routed mutation, coordinator query options) targets system partitions, now structural. REPAIR_ELIGIBLE routing of a user partition exists only in a test. Construction contract (fixture-migration fidelity condition): QueryExecutor and SqlQueryEngine no longer default an absent readiness owner to eligible. Without controlPlaneReadinessService, serve routing answers the typed unavailability; it never fails open. Production composition wires the owner through startup. Two sites can still build an engine with readiness '|| null': src/cluster/node-joining-publication-activation.js:628 and src/control-plane/seed-runtime-bridge-owner.js:51. Serve inputs changed in attempt 1: the message-group service row is no longer an input to the serve decision (serve = committed lease + published membership + acks + priority spread + owner load-ready). Load-readiness (the readiness owner's isNodeLoadReady) was added to the committed answer, so a heartbeat with saturating load closes serving at once (readiness-routing-heartbeat-window witness).

Frozen-oracle supersessions (R09, recorded differential): readiness-admission-transitions-observed digests re-baselined ab030311... -> 4ec68886... with recorded per-decision source-read call counts; readiness-routing-denial-observability digest re-baselined to ed83521a... on DENIAL_ROUTING_DIMENSION 'controlPlaneRecoveryEligible'. Cause in both: serve is the committed answer, so routing no longer reads projected serve evidence. formation-release-handoff fixture: a host counts as routable when its connectionState is connected (transport only, D2).

Planning-owner hazard (pre-existing, found while debugging a test hang on attempt 1): when a composition has a nodesOwner but its cache has no getTableMutationVersion, readPlanningProjectionIdentity is saturated forever. Every completed build is then refused while tokenCurrent stays true, and handleStaleCompletion (readiness-planning-completion-admission-methods.js:590) re-enqueues a LIVE_VETO rebuild on each setImmediate, an unbounded macrotask loop (about 11k rebuilds in 4 s). Production caches carry mutation versions, so the loop is reachable only from such a fixture. The test was fixed by stopping the service at teardown and using a committed view. The loop itself is not bounded: this is a candidate for the planning-owner quest, not fixed here.

Lead sequencing for attempt 2 (F10 CREATE TABLE contract): Stream B's attempt 2 deletes the CREATE TABLE projection-visibility wait (allowPendingVisibility / visibilityState). It routes CREATE TABLE's only remaining pending answer through the existing provisioning-convergence owner, keeping today's contractState / nextAction words; F10 owns the vocabulary change (UNDER_REPLICATED etc., owner-approved). Attempt 2 starts from Stream B's landed head (branch work/replica-admission-committed-operation-20261102; the lead sends the SHA) and states D1 in F10 terms there. No projection read is re-introduced on the CREATE TABLE answer path.

Census finding routed from Stream B by the lead. sendHeartbeat (node-lifecycle publication) is a full-row NODES merge read from the projection. It re-publishes columns owned by 14 other writers (failure-detector, lease-service, node-registration, reintegration, storage-budget, capacity-migration, group-selection, latency-group-manager, membership-publication runtime owner, replica-create-admission, joining delegates/backfill, query-system-state), so a stale projection read can overwrite a newer committed field (lost update). Lease expiry over other nodes' rows (publication-methods ~561) and reintegration also decide from the projection (C7). Repair shape recorded by the lead: column ownership. Each writer updates only its own columns through the partial conditional UPDATE; the heartbeat touches only heartbeat columns and reads nothing; CAS only where a column has two writers; other-row decisions come from committed reads or are declared observation-only. Placement: attempt 3, with C7 (rebalancer settle from committed rows), after F10 in attempt 2. It shares the committed nodes read and the lease-expiry CAS with the C7 decisions.

Attempt 1 (owner read + epoch memo, serve routing, system-table routing on leadership, carve-out deletions). Owner: src/control-plane/serve-eligibility-owner.js + control-plane-readiness-serve-eligibility-methods.js on ControlPlaneReadinessService: committed read of nodes and the latest PUBLISHED cluster_membership control_plane_publications row through AuthoritativeControlPlaneView.readReadinessOwnerRows (OWNER_RPC_REQUIRED, leader REQUIRED, READINESS_INTERNAL); answer {state ready, decision eligible|not_eligible, reasons, epoch{publicationEpoch, publicationId, readAtMs}, leaseExpiresAtMs} or {state unavailable, reason unavailable_stale|committed_read_failed|no_committed_record|committed_read_pending|owner_stopped, epoch, retryAfterMs = the committed read's own deadline}; memo keyed by epoch; cache events are triggers only (newer epoch or a revoking node change -> stale + refresh; a lease extension -> background refresh, answer stays valid); a positive answer never outlives its committed lease (refresh armed at the earliest lease expiry). The SERVE_ELIGIBLE dimension and the projection serve lane carry only the owner answer (serve-lane publication-stream and priority-recovery blockers removed: those facts are in the committed answer); a new epoch re-keys planning snapshots (owner dependency serveEligibilityOwner) and stored snapshots. User-table serve routing consumes answerServeEligibility; an all-denied serve snapshot awaits one owner refresh then re-decides. System-table routing (every system partition) = every active, addressed replica is a candidate; no readiness and no transport filter in the candidate set (D2: the delivery layer applies live transport - reconnect deferral, fall-through - and the target proves leadership: witness / typed redirect / NOT_LEADER).
